title: Scalable Uncertainty Quantification for Extreme Weather Forecasting via Empirical Neural Tangent Kernels

problem.claim: Deep learning weather models produce deterministic forecasts without uncertainty estimates, limiting their use for high-stakes decisions during extreme weather events.

gap.claim: A scalable approach is needed to provide uncertainty estimates for fast deep learning weather forecasts while adapting to extreme-event severity.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes NTK-UQ using last-layer empirical features for uncertainty quantification.
Theoretical analysis identifies architecture-dependent effects on uncertainty quality through variance collapse and decomposition performance.
The framework performs inference-time uncertainty estimation without retraining and requires one matrix-vector product per sample.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed selection rule correctly prescribes ICA or SVD for all four evaluated architectures.
Compared with split conformal prediction, NTK-UQ achieves 31–37% sharper prediction intervals at 90% coverage.
NTK-UQ produces adaptive intervals that scale with extreme-event severity, whereas conformal prediction cannot do so by construction.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fast deep learning weather forecasts lack uncertainty estimates needed for high-stakes extreme-weather decisions.
The paper introduces NTK-UQ based on last-layer empirical features.
The analysis explains architecture-dependent uncertainty quality through variance collapse and the suitability of ICA or SVD for heavy-tailed extreme-weather features.
A feature-eigenspectrum concentration ratio selects between ICA and SVD.
The method is reported to improve interval sharpness and adaptivity over split conformal prediction without retraining, with low inference cost.

source_observation.claim: Uncertainty quality depends on feature-spectrum concentration and decomposition performance depends on heavy-tailed structure.

interpretation.claim: Uncertainty estimation methods may need architecture- and data-structure-aware decomposition choices rather than a uniform approximation.

application.claim: For extreme-event forecasting, inspect eigenspectrum concentration and consider ICA when higher-order, heavy-tailed structure is important.

exception.claim: The reported selection rule and performance apply only to the four evaluated architectures and the described setting.

source_observation.claim: NTK-UQ is reported to produce severity-adaptive intervals without retraining at inference time.

interpretation.claim: Post-hoc uncertainty methods can provide operationally useful adaptivity when retraining is impractical.

application.claim: Deploy inference-time uncertainty estimation for high-stakes forecasting workflows where retraining or extensive additional computation is undesirable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance or computational behavior outside the evaluated architectures and comparison setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, geographic coverage, forecast horizons, or event definitions.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, uncertainty-calibration results beyond the stated coverage, or comparisons with additional baselines.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported empirical findings.
